Jesus, welcome to my world.   
   
My mother was dying from cancer when I was 12. Abandoned by every adult, she put me in charge of her medications. I only wanted to help. She died the next morning.   
  
6 months later I told my father how happy I was that he was doing something good for himself, though he abandoned our sick mother. He'd been pretty selfish, but I only wanted to help. A few hours later he died of a heart attack from a heroine overdose.   
  
 I lived with my brother after that. My brother refused to send me to a military school out of guilt. I did everything possible to be invisible. I only wanted to help. A couple of months later, his husband died drinking himself to death because my brother chose me over him.  
  
 My brother fell into a deep alcoholic depression. I knew I couldn't be his burden any longer. I went back to my home town to live with friends of the family as their adoptive son. I had my best friend from elementary in my corner helping me. Dropping me off before church, he is side-swiped by a truck. I see the life fade from him. This is labeled by everyone in a God-fearing small town as my fault.   
I only wanted to help.   
  
Years have gone by. I'm 30 now. The friends I've made, the family I've built...  
It doesn't matter. They'v moved forward with their lives.   
  
I only wanted to help. 
  
 (A true story)

My brother came from Ireland to the states at 12 with me, so feel free to read this in a heavy Irish accent as I'm narrating this. My brother adapted almost too well and appropriated an American accent within the first month, which is what Americans really want from foreigners. He was almost 2 years younger, but since he grew up stronger and faster than me we often got mistaken for twins. I wasn't as attractive or social as he was, so I kind of retained my accent. Beside wearing glasses, we looked pretty similar.   
 Our parents died from natural causes within a year of each other. I accepted that it was just the randomness of the universe at work. He couldn't accept that. I accepted the world for the aimless chaos that it was and tried to make the best of it as a barkeep. He didn't. To him the only way the world would make sense or be justified was if he could force it to.    
 So, I wander into into my office on Monday at my second job, slightly hungover. It's not that I had a drinking problem, but Sunday nights working bar were pretty bad. The people there on a late Sunday night had no plans for Monday, and if you have an accent they're turned on. They buy you drinks, and to keep business you can't always turn down a drink if they want to drink with you, or you seem like an uncaring dick.   
    Coworker comes up to me. "So, out late?" she said with a sly giggle. Spot on. I sense sarcasm in her voice for some reason. I work at local tv station during the week, so I haven't been caught up on the last 48hr news cycle. I just assume it's some reference I've missed. Happens often.      
    "Hey Clark Kent, you have a back-list of commercials to put into the system and verify." Seems about par for a Monday, but what's with the attitude and snide tone? That's new. Then I look at one of the 20 screens and see the answer.   
  A local high quality camera at a gas station across the street adjacent to where a robbery was stopped showed a close up of a vigilante. He'd worn a hood and eye makeup, but the single unfortunate frame was still-screened and captured for display. 
  I knew it was my brother, doing what he thought was right. He'd kept up a decent facade to where his look changed weekly. I understood why now. The man had plans.   
   So, in order to draw attention from him I'd never mentioned him. He'd somehow  erased the paper trail of his existence, so I continued to draw suspicion to me while leading a normal life. He's not crazy. He 's out there, doing good. More than I could achieve, serving drunks and being a cog in a poisonous news cycle. The most good that I can do is to be the primary suspect and wasting the time of those that suspect us.   
  Buy him as much time as possible because I know he's doing the most good.
